jobs.title: Director, Platform Systems
jobs.description:
Opentext - The Information Company

OpenText is a global leader in information management, where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are the key components of our corporate culture. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to partner with the most highly regarded companies in the world, tackle complex issues, and contribute to projects that shape the future of digital transformation.

AI-First. Future-Driven. Human-Centered.

At OpenText, AI is at the heart of everything we do—powering innovation, transforming work, and empowering digital knowledge workers. We are hiring talent AI can't replace to help us shape the future of information management. Join us.

YOUR IMPACT

OpenText is looking for an experienced and collaborative technology leader to join our Corporate IT organization as Director, Platform Systems
. In this global leadership role, you will be responsible for the strategy, delivery, and operational excellence of critical enterprise capabilities across Integration Systems, Security and Identity Access Management, and Fulfillment Systems. You will lead distributed teams, partner with business and technology stakeholders, and help modernize the systems and practices that enable secure, scalable, and efficient business operations.

What The Role Offers

Leading and influencing in a global, matrixed environment with teams and stakeholders across multiple regions.
Manage budgets, vendor relationships, licensing decisions, and platform investments with a focus on business value, simplification, and cost effectiveness.
Work with technologies that may include Cloud Integration Hub/ICDM, SAP PI/PO, SAP Integration Suite/BTP, Boomi, MuleSoft, Google Cloud Platform, IAM platforms, licensing and fulfillment systems, APIs, automation, and observability tools.
Building trusted relationships with business partners, technology leaders, architects, cybersecurity teams, infrastructure teams, vendors, and consultants.
Communicating clearly with executive, business, technical, and operational audiences.
Bringing structure, transparency, and prioritization to complex portfolios of work.
Driving Agile ways of working, delivery predictability, team accountability, and continuous improvement.
Applying AI and automation thoughtfully to improve speed, quality, operational insight, documentation, testing, and productivity.
Balancing strategic planning with hands-on leadership in a fast-paced, business-critical environment.
Simplifying technology landscapes, reducing risk, improving resilience, and aligning work to measurable outcomes.
Promoting strong development, integration, security, identity, fulfillment, documentation, and operational practices.
Staying current on emerging trends in integration platforms, IAM, application security, fulfillment, cloud, APIs, AI, and automation.

What You Need To Succeed

10+ years of progressive experience leading application, development, enterprise systems, integration, security, identity, fulfillment, or platform teams.
Demonstrated experience leading global teams, managing multiple workstreams, and delivering business-critical technology services.
Strong technical leadership experience across enterprise integration platforms, API management, cloud integration, SAP integration technologies, IAM tools, fulfillment or licensing systems, and modern application delivery practices.
Agile training or certification is required; hands-on experience leading Agile teams, Scrum practices, backlog management, delivery metrics, and Agile maturity improvement is strongly preferred.
Working knowledge of AI capabilities and practical use cases in Integration, Security, Identity Management, and Fulfillment Systems, including automation, developer productivity, observability, testing, application security, and operational efficiency.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to translate technical complexity into clear business language.
Strong people leadership skills, including coaching, performance management, talent development, succession planning, and building engaged teams.
Strong analytical, negotiation, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, matrixed environment while maintaining delivery discipline, operational rigor, and stakeholder confidence.
Experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, enterprise transformation, or major technology modernization initiatives is an asset.
High-tech software or enterprise software industry experience is an asset.
A relevant bachelor’s or master’s degree, college diploma, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

One Last Thing

OpenText is more than just a corporation, it's a global community where trust is foundational, the bar is raised, and outcomes are owned.

Join us on our mission to drive positive change through privacy, technology, and collaboration. At OpenText, we don't just have a culture; we have character. Choose us because you want to be part of a company that embraces innovation and empowers its employees to make a difference.

OpenText's commitment to diversity and inclusion surpasses legal requirements, evident in our Equal Employment Opportunity Statement of Policy which promotes a respectful and empowering environment for employees of all backgrounds, culture, national origin, race, color, gender, gender identification, sexual orientation, family status, age, veteran status, disability, religion, or other basis protected by applicable laws.

If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please submit a ticket at Ask HR. Our proactive approach fosters collaboration, innovation, and personal growth, enriching OpenText's vibrant workplace.

Compensation:
At OpenText, we offer a thoughtfully designed benefits package that supports your physical, emotional, and financial wellbeing. As you move through the hiring process, we’re happy to provide more details about our compensation programs, including variable and commission compensation opportunities for eligible roles, vacation entitlement, and paid time off.

Salary Range:
Depending on the candidate’s education, experience, skills, geographical location, and alignment with internal equity and external market, actual salary may vary and be higher or lower than the range posted.

AI Usage Disclosure:
As part of our commitment to transparency, we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in various stages of our recruitment process, including resume screening, candidate matching, interview scheduling, and communications. These tools are designed to improve efficiency, reduce bias, and enhance candidate experience. All decisions regarding hiring are made by qualified human professionals, and we continuously monitor our AI systems to ensure fairness and compliance with applicable regulations.

jobs.description:
Location

Brookfield Place - 181 Bay Street

Brookfield Culture

Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture. We seek team members who have a long-term focus and whose values align with our Attributes of a Brookfield Leader: Entrepreneurial, Collaborative and Disciplined. Brookfield is committed to the development of our people through challenging work assignments and exposure to diverse businesses.

Job Description

Position Summary

The Director, Internal Audit Analytics & Artificial Intelligence leads the Audit Analytics and AI function within Internal Audit, driving the adoption of data analytics, automation and emerging technologies to enhance audit quality, efficiency, and insight generation.

Reporting to the Audit and Analytics SVP, the Director partners closely with audit leaders and business stakeholders, both from Brookfield and Portfolio Companies, to integrate analytics and AI across the audit lifecycle, identify opportunities for innovation, and develop scalable solutions that strengthen the Internal Audit function. This role combines technical expertise with strong leadership, requiring excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Strategy

Lead the continued development and execution of the Internal Audit Analytics & AI strategy and roadmap.
Identify opportunities to expand analytics, automation, and AI across audit engagements.
Lead and develop a high-performing analytics team while fostering collaboration and innovation.
Establish priorities and best practices for analytics and AI within Internal Audit.

Audit Analytics & AI

Lead the integration of analytics throughout the audit lifecycle.
Oversee scalable analytics to identify risks, anomalies, and control weaknesses.
Drive the evaluation and implementation of AI, generative AI, process mining, and intelligent automation.
Promote responsible AI practices aligned with governance expectations.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Partner with audit leadership, Technology, Finance, Risk, and business stakeholders.
Present analytical findings and recommendations to senior management.

Technology Leadership

Support scalable data architecture and visualization capabilities.

People Leadership

Mentor and develop analytics professionals.
Promote knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.
Support capability development.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Accounting or a related field.

Experience

10+ years of progressive experience in Audit Analytics and AI, Digital and AI Transformation.
Experience leading analytics initiatives and managing teams.
Experience presenting insights to senior management.

Strategic thinker with strong business acumen.
Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to influence without direct authority.
Strong project management and organizational skills.
Passion for innovation and emerging technologies.

jobs.title: Director, Development Finance & Accounting
jobs.description:
Cortel Group | Vaughan, Ontario

Employment Type:
Full-Time, Permanent
Experience:
8–12+ Years
Reports To:
Company Leadership & Partners
About Cortel Group

Cortel Group is an established real estate development company specializing in high-rise residential condominiums, commercial developments, and purpose-built rental communities throughout the Greater Toronto Area.

We are seeking an experienced, analytical, and proactive Director, Development Finance & Accounting
to lead the financial management of our development portfolio, oversee accounting operations, and provide strategic financial guidance directly to company leadership and partners.

This is a hands-on leadership position combining real estate development finance, project feasibility analysis, financial reporting, and team management. The successful candidate will play an important role in evaluating development opportunities, monitoring project performance, identifying financial risks, and improving the effectiveness of the Finance Department.

Key Responsibilities

Development Finance & Feasibility Analysis

Lead financial feasibility assessments for prospective and existing real estate development projects.
Develop, maintain, and evaluate detailed development pro formas, financial models, cash flow projections, and investment return analyses.
Conduct sensitivity and scenario analyses to assess the impact of changes in construction costs, development charges, financing rates, sales prices, rental rates, absorption, and project timelines.
Evaluate project profitability, financial viability, capital requirements, and investment risks.
Provide financial analysis, recommendations, and strategic insights directly to company leadership and partners to support acquisition, development, financing, and investment decisions.
Review and challenge project assumptions, identifying potential risks and opportunities to improve financial outcomes.

Project Financial Management & Oversight

Oversee financial management and reporting across multiple real estate development projects.
Manage development budgets, cost tracking, cash flow forecasts, financial commitments, and variance analyses.
Monitor project financial performance throughout the development lifecycle, from acquisition and construction through occupancy, stabilization, and final closing.
Oversee construction financing, lender reporting, and construction draw requirements.
Identify budget discrepancies, financial exposures, and opportunities for cost optimization.
Prepare and present timely, accurate financial reports and project performance updates to company leadership and partners.

Accounting & Team Leadership

Lead, supervise, and mentor accounting personnel, ensuring accountability, accuracy, and timely completion of deliverables.
Oversee financial reporting, reconciliations, intercompany transactions, and accounting across multiple corporate entities.
Maintain strong financial controls and ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate with internal departments, financial institutions, auditors, legal advisors, and external consultants.
Establish clear reporting expectations, performance standards, and accountability within the accounting team.

Financial Reporting & Process Improvement

Evaluate existing financial reporting procedures, accounting systems, and project tracking processes.
Identify and implement opportunities to streamline workflows, improve accuracy, and increase departmental efficiency.
Develop consistent reporting frameworks that provide leadership with clear visibility into project budgets, cash flow, profitability, and financial risks.
Strengthen internal controls, reporting timelines, and financial accountability.
Proactively recommend improvements to financial management practices and operational processes.

Qualifications & Experience

8–12+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, preferably within real estate development or construction.
Significant experience in high-rise residential development accounting and finance; exposure to commercial and purpose-built rental developments is an asset.
Demonstrated experience preparing development feasibility studies, financial models, sensitivity analyses, and project cash flow forecasts.
Strong understanding of real estate development economics, construction financing, development costs, and investment return metrics.
Proven experience managing multiple project budgets and overseeing financial reporting across multiple corporate entities.
Demonstrated leadership experience supervising and developing accounting personnel.
Strong financial modelling capabilities and advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
Experience implementing improvements to financial reporting, accounting systems, and internal processes.
Excellent analytical, organizational, communication, and problem-solving abilities.
Ability to independently evaluate financial information, challenge assumptions, and present clear recommendations to senior leadership.
Degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA designation is preferred.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for a commercially minded, hands-on financial leader who takes ownership, exercises sound judgment, and proactively identifies opportunities to improve financial performance and operational efficiency.
The successful candidate will combine technical accounting expertise with a strong understanding of real estate development economics and investment analysis.
They will be comfortable working directly with company leadership and partners, providing thoughtful financial insights, challenging assumptions, and contributing to important business and investment decisions.
Equally important, this individual will demonstrate strong leadership, accountability, attention to detail, and the ability to develop a high-performing accounting team.

Why Join Cortel Group?

This is an opportunity to assume a key leadership position within an established real estate development company, with direct exposure to company leadership and meaningful involvement in development and investment decisions.
The successful candidate will contribute to the financial oversight of a diverse development portfolio while helping shape and improve the systems, processes, and financial reporting practices that support the company's continued growth.

How to Apply

Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume outlining their relevant experience and qualifications.
We thank all applicants for their interest. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Director of Finance and Administration
jobs.description:
Position:
                   Director of Finance and Administration
Location:
                  Martin Luther University College, Waterloo, Ontario
Hours:                        
Full-time, 35 hours per week, 8:30am to 4:30pm, In office at least 4 days a week   
Reports to:
               Principal-Dean
Direct Reports:          
1 - 2 roles        
Salary:
                        $90,000 - $120,000 annually     
Start date
:                  December 2026

This is an existing vacancy.

Position Summary

Martin Luther University College (Luther) is a public university college federated with Wilfrid Laurier University. We are a faith-based academic community committed to excellence in teaching, research, and community engagement.

The Director of Finance and Administration provides strategic and operational leadership for Luther’s financial and administrative functions. Reporting to the Principal-Dean, the Director is responsible for financial reporting, compliance, planning and budgeting, internal controls, and administrative systems that support the long-term financial sustainability of the institution and its mission.

Responsibilities

Leadership of Financial Planning, Management, and Reporting

Ensure all necessary financial operations (including the operating budget), reporting, cash management, expenditure controls and other controls are in place and operating effectively to support Luther’s operations and the Board’s fiduciary obligations.
Prepare financial analysis and reports as needed including operating statements (revenues and expenditures), budget forecasts, and forecast of cash flow for use by the Principal-Dean, responsible managers or faculty, and the Finance Committee to support informed decision-making and organizational accountability for a $4 Million operating budget.
Manage the allocation of annual realized gains from endowment funds and reconcile investment manager’s reports for endowed and non-endowed investments, resolving discrepancies.
Take the initiative to manage investment transactions required as part of the annual budget or operations. Coordinate the flow of investment deposits and investment income with investment manager. Liaise with Luther’s investment manager and/or Finance Committee on investment issues for accounting purposes.
Prepare annual unaudited financial statements and all reconciliations, supporting schedules, background reporting, and year end entries and adjustments required for the annual audit; prepare an audit package and manage the annual audit with the external auditors once per year, including: Schedule the audit and associated activities, Negotiate the audit contract for recommendation to the Finance Committee, Manage Luther’s elements of the process, Ensure a clean audit
Assist Luther’s staff and faculty in understanding and using relevant financial information. Support them in budget development for their areas or projects.
Understand in detail and make recommendations to enhance the funding agreements between Luther and Wilfrid Laurier University and be able to advise the Principal-Dean on the implications to annual revenue of proposed revisions to these agreements.
Maximize the use of accounting software reporting capabilities where possible.
Manage the financial elements of grant projects, supporting the assigned project manager in planning and tracking financial commitments, and in financial reporting for the project.
Prepare and submit annual financial and statistical reporting required by external organizations such as Canada Revenue Agency (Registered Charity Information Return -- T3010, HST), Council of Ontario Universities (detailed analytical financial report), Association of Theological Schools, and others as required. Consult with these organizations regarding reporting requirements as necessary. 
Develop the annual capital budget (including equipment) for Board approval to maintain the Luther’s physical assets and avoid undue deferred maintenance.
Oversee the implementation of the capital budget.
Manage the financial elements of capital and construction projects.

General Administration

Act as the Chief Compliance Officer for reporting and legal requirements.

Policy Coordination and Board Support

Coordinate policy needs and improvements with the Principal-Dean to ensure all operational and board policies are consistently organized, reviewed, updated, and in compliance.

Support to the Principal-Dean

Support the activities of the Principal-Dean through research, high-level project/program development and implementation, implementation of confidential activities and other areas as they arise from time to time.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field
CPA designation
A minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in finance or accounting
A minimum of 3 years of leadership or management experience
Ability to lead strategically while maintaining hands-on responsibility for day-to-day financial and administrative operations in a lean organizational environment
Ability to work effectively within a governance-based environment, supporting boards and collaborating with diverse interest holders
Experience in a post-secondary institution, public sector, or medium non-profit organization is preferred
Strong knowledge of public sector and/or fund accounting
Advanced financial planning, budgeting, and analytical skills
Ability to communicate complete financial information clearly to non-financial interest holders
Strong leadership, collaboration and relationship-management skills
High level of integrity, judgment, and professional discretion
Experience with enterprise resource planning and financial reporting systems

Working Conditions

This position is based primarily in an in-office environment and requires regular on-site presence during standard business hours. The role involves extended periods of computer work, frequent interaction with staff, leadership and external partners, and coordination of multiple operational priorities. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required to support meetings or organizational needs. The position requires the ability to manage competing deadlines, maintain confidentiality, and respond to evolving organizational priorities in a collaborative workplace setting.

This role requires extended periods of sitting and computer use, including keyboarding and screen work. The position may involve light physical activity such as moving between office spaces, attending meetings, and occasionally lifting or moving materials (up to approximately 10–20 lbs). The ability to communicate effectively in person and through digital platforms is required.

TO APPLY

To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter in one file
to search@luther.wlu.ca by November 4, 2026
. Please insert “Director of Finance and Administration”
in the subject line.

Candidates selected for an interview will be required to provide three professional references.

The organization is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible workplace. Reasonable accommodation will be provided throughout the recruitment process and employment in accordance with applicable accessibility and human rights legislation.

Martin Luther University College is committed to diversity and creating a culture of inclusion by increasing the diversity of faculty and staff and welcomes applications from qualified members of the equity-deserving groups. The College welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race nationality, gender-affiliation or sexual orientation.  All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.

Candidate provided information is used for recruitment purposes only and will not be shared with outside agencies. Information will be retained for a minimum of two years for the sole purpose of applicant review and future recruitment.

Terms of Appointment:

This is a management position as an employee of Martin Luther University College. Luther employees are not employees of Wilfrid Laurier University.

ABOUT LUTHER

Martin Luther University College (formerly Waterloo Lutheran Seminary) is in Waterloo, Ontario and federated with Wilfrid Laurier University. As a federated college, Luther has its own Board of Governors which oversees the work of the institution, supporting its mission of education for a life of meaning and service through spiritually integrated education. Luther offers academic programming at the undergraduate, graduate, and graduate diploma levels. Our small class sizes and dedicated learning space help create a special sense of community where people connect closely with each other.

Students

Approximately 250 students are enrolled in Luther’s programs at any one time, and another 300 undergraduate students, registered at Wilfrid Laurier University, enroll in Luther courses as electives. Luther students come from a variety of different faith traditions while some have no faith tradition at all.

Faculty & Staff

Luther is comprised of thirteen full- and part-time faculty members, along with approximately 20 adjunct faculty who teach on a term-by-term basis. The school is supported by a team of eight full-time staff members working in communications, student services, and administration departments, and another 10 staff members working in part-time and program-related positions.

Centres at Martin Luther University College

The Centres of Luther offer programming at the intersection of scholarship and community engagement. Administratively, the Centres fall within Luther’s finance and administration portfolio, which supports their operations. Our largest centre is The Glebe Counselling Centre, a not-for-profit, multifaith counselling agency committed to strengthening emotional and spiritual well-being.

jobs.description:
SETUP

About the Opportunity

Financial Reporting & Consolidations:
Lead the preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, and annual consolidated financial statements and management reporting.
Oversee the consolidation of multiple legal entities/business units, including intercompany balances, eliminations, foreign currency translation, and consolidation adjustments.
Ensure financial reporting is accurate, complete, appropriately supported, and delivered within established reporting timelines.
Maintain and enhance consolidation processes, reporting packages, and financial controls.
Partner with business units and finance teams to resolve consolidation and reporting issues.

US GAAP & IFRS:
Serve as a key technical accounting resource for matters involving US GAAP and IFRS.
Research and assess complex accounting issues and provide recommendations regarding appropriate accounting treatment.
Monitor new and emerging accounting standards and assess their impact on the organization.
Lead the implementation of new accounting standards and changes to existing reporting requirements.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos, position papers, and supporting documentation.
Support accounting matters involving areas such as revenue recognition, leases, business combinations, foreign currency, impairment, and other complex transactions, as applicable.

Controls, Audit & Compliance:
Maintain a strong financial control environment across the reporting and consolidation processes.
Coordinate with internal and external auditors and support quarterly and annual audit requirements.
Ensure appropriate documentation and supporting schedules are maintained for significant accounting judgments, estimates, and transactions.
Identify reporting and control risks and implement process improvements to strengthen financial governance.
Leadership & Business Partnership:
Lead, coach, and develop a team of 4–5 finance and accounting professionals, establishing clear responsibilities and development priorities.
Provide technical guidance and oversight to the team while promoting accountability and high-quality execution.
Partner closely with FP&A, Corporate Accounting, Tax, Treasury, and other finance functions to ensure consistency and accuracy across financial reporting.
Work with senior leadership to communicate financial reporting matters, accounting implications, and significant issues.
Support acquisitions, integrations, restructuring activities, and other strategic initiatives from an accounting and reporting perspective.

Process Improvement:
Drive improvements to the financial close, consolidation, and reporting processes with a focus on accuracy, efficiency, standardization, and scalability.
Identify opportunities to automate manual reporting and reconciliation activities.
Strengthen reporting processes, systems, and controls as the organization grows and reporting requirements evolve.

About You

CPA designation.
10+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, including significant experience in a leadership capacity.
Strong technical knowledge and practical application of US GAAP and/or IFRS.
Significant experience with multi-entity consolidations, including intercompany eliminations and foreign currency considerations.
Experience leading and developing accounting or financial reporting teams.

Our Cutting-edge SaaS Solutions Empower Revenue Leaders Globally To Design Smarter Go-to-market Strategies, Maximize Seller Performance, And Unlock Untapped Potential. Here’s Why You’ll Thrive At Varicent

Innovate with Purpose: Build impactful solutions for customers worldwide.
Join Excellence: Work in a diverse, collaborative, and innovative team.

Grow Together: Unlock your potential in a supportive environment.

Join us at Varicent—where your talent and ambition meet limitless opportunities for success!

The Opportunity

Varicent is seeking a strategic, creative, and data-driven Director, Digital Marketing & Web Experience
to lead our digital growth engine across digital marketing, website strategy and experience, paid media, SEO/AEO/GEO, conversion optimization, and digital performance measurement.

This leader will own the strategy and performance of Varicent’s digital channels, with accountability for their contribution to pipeline and revenue. You’ll lead a team and agency ecosystem spanning digital marketing and web experience while partnering closely with Marketing leadership, Demand Generation, Product Marketing, Content, Creative, Marketing Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales, Customer Marketing, IT, Finance, and other stakeholders.

What You’ll Do

Digital Marketing Strategy & Leadership

We’re looking for a digital leader who has operated in a B2B SaaS, technology, enterprise software, or similarly complex sales environment

12+ years of experience across digital marketing, growth, demand generation, performance marketing, or web strategy.
7+ years of people leadership experience, including leading multidisciplinary teams or managers.
Experience owning digital strategy with measurable responsibility for pipeline, revenue, conversion, and customer acquisition.
Deep knowledge of paid media, SEO/SEM, digital acquisition, web strategy, CRO, analytics, and experimentation.

Experience with HubSpot CMS, ABM and intent platforms, multi-touch attribution, website personalization, CRO platforms, behavioral analytics, major website redesigns or migrations, and global digital programs

new_jobs.title: Director of Finance and Administration
new_jobs.description:
Position:
                   Director of Finance and Administration
Location:
                  Martin Luther University College, Waterloo, Ontario
Hours:                        
Full-time, 35 hours per week, 8:30am to 4:30pm, In office at least 4 days a week   
Reports to:
               Principal-Dean
Direct Reports:          
1 - 2 roles        
Salary:
                        $90,000 - $120,000 annually     
Start date
:                  December 2026

This is an existing vacancy.

Position Summary

Martin Luther University College (Luther) is a public university college federated with Wilfrid Laurier University. We are a faith-based academic community committed to excellence in teaching, research, and community engagement.

The Director of Finance and Administration provides strategic and operational leadership for Luther’s financial and administrative functions. Reporting to the Principal-Dean, the Director is responsible for financial reporting, compliance, planning and budgeting, internal controls, and administrative systems that support the long-term financial sustainability of the institution and its mission.

Responsibilities

Leadership of Financial Planning, Management, and Reporting

Ensure all necessary financial operations (including the operating budget), reporting, cash management, expenditure controls and other controls are in place and operating effectively to support Luther’s operations and the Board’s fiduciary obligations.
Prepare financial analysis and reports as needed including operating statements (revenues and expenditures), budget forecasts, and forecast of cash flow for use by the Principal-Dean, responsible managers or faculty, and the Finance Committee to support informed decision-making and organizational accountability for a $4 Million operating budget.
Manage the allocation of annual realized gains from endowment funds and reconcile investment manager’s reports for endowed and non-endowed investments, resolving discrepancies.
Take the initiative to manage investment transactions required as part of the annual budget or operations. Coordinate the flow of investment deposits and investment income with investment manager. Liaise with Luther’s investment manager and/or Finance Committee on investment issues for accounting purposes.
Prepare annual unaudited financial statements and all reconciliations, supporting schedules, background reporting, and year end entries and adjustments required for the annual audit; prepare an audit package and manage the annual audit with the external auditors once per year, including: Schedule the audit and associated activities, Negotiate the audit contract for recommendation to the Finance Committee, Manage Luther’s elements of the process, Ensure a clean audit
Assist Luther’s staff and faculty in understanding and using relevant financial information. Support them in budget development for their areas or projects.
Understand in detail and make recommendations to enhance the funding agreements between Luther and Wilfrid Laurier University and be able to advise the Principal-Dean on the implications to annual revenue of proposed revisions to these agreements.
Maximize the use of accounting software reporting capabilities where possible.
Manage the financial elements of grant projects, supporting the assigned project manager in planning and tracking financial commitments, and in financial reporting for the project.
Prepare and submit annual financial and statistical reporting required by external organizations such as Canada Revenue Agency (Registered Charity Information Return -- T3010, HST), Council of Ontario Universities (detailed analytical financial report), Association of Theological Schools, and others as required. Consult with these organizations regarding reporting requirements as necessary. 
Develop the annual capital budget (including equipment) for Board approval to maintain the Luther’s physical assets and avoid undue deferred maintenance.
Oversee the implementation of the capital budget.
Manage the financial elements of capital and construction projects.

General Administration

Act as the Chief Compliance Officer for reporting and legal requirements.

Policy Coordination and Board Support

Coordinate policy needs and improvements with the Principal-Dean to ensure all operational and board policies are consistently organized, reviewed, updated, and in compliance.

Support to the Principal-Dean

Support the activities of the Principal-Dean through research, high-level project/program development and implementation, implementation of confidential activities and other areas as they arise from time to time.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field
CPA designation
A minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in finance or accounting
A minimum of 3 years of leadership or management experience
Ability to lead strategically while maintaining hands-on responsibility for day-to-day financial and administrative operations in a lean organizational environment
Ability to work effectively within a governance-based environment, supporting boards and collaborating with diverse interest holders
Experience in a post-secondary institution, public sector, or medium non-profit organization is preferred
Strong knowledge of public sector and/or fund accounting
Advanced financial planning, budgeting, and analytical skills
Ability to communicate complete financial information clearly to non-financial interest holders
Strong leadership, collaboration and relationship-management skills
High level of integrity, judgment, and professional discretion
Experience with enterprise resource planning and financial reporting systems

Working Conditions

This position is based primarily in an in-office environment and requires regular on-site presence during standard business hours. The role involves extended periods of computer work, frequent interaction with staff, leadership and external partners, and coordination of multiple operational priorities. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required to support meetings or organizational needs. The position requires the ability to manage competing deadlines, maintain confidentiality, and respond to evolving organizational priorities in a collaborative workplace setting.

This role requires extended periods of sitting and computer use, including keyboarding and screen work. The position may involve light physical activity such as moving between office spaces, attending meetings, and occasionally lifting or moving materials (up to approximately 10–20 lbs). The ability to communicate effectively in person and through digital platforms is required.

TO APPLY

To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter in one file
to search@luther.wlu.ca by November 4, 2026
. Please insert “Director of Finance and Administration”
in the subject line.

Candidates selected for an interview will be required to provide three professional references.

The organization is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible workplace. Reasonable accommodation will be provided throughout the recruitment process and employment in accordance with applicable accessibility and human rights legislation.

Martin Luther University College is committed to diversity and creating a culture of inclusion by increasing the diversity of faculty and staff and welcomes applications from qualified members of the equity-deserving groups. The College welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race nationality, gender-affiliation or sexual orientation.  All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.

Candidate provided information is used for recruitment purposes only and will not be shared with outside agencies. Information will be retained for a minimum of two years for the sole purpose of applicant review and future recruitment.

Terms of Appointment:

This is a management position as an employee of Martin Luther University College. Luther employees are not employees of Wilfrid Laurier University.

ABOUT LUTHER

Martin Luther University College (formerly Waterloo Lutheran Seminary) is in Waterloo, Ontario and federated with Wilfrid Laurier University. As a federated college, Luther has its own Board of Governors which oversees the work of the institution, supporting its mission of education for a life of meaning and service through spiritually integrated education. Luther offers academic programming at the undergraduate, graduate, and graduate diploma levels. Our small class sizes and dedicated learning space help create a special sense of community where people connect closely with each other.

Students

Approximately 250 students are enrolled in Luther’s programs at any one time, and another 300 undergraduate students, registered at Wilfrid Laurier University, enroll in Luther courses as electives. Luther students come from a variety of different faith traditions while some have no faith tradition at all.

Faculty & Staff

Luther is comprised of thirteen full- and part-time faculty members, along with approximately 20 adjunct faculty who teach on a term-by-term basis. The school is supported by a team of eight full-time staff members working in communications, student services, and administration departments, and another 10 staff members working in part-time and program-related positions.

Centres at Martin Luther University College

The Centres of Luther offer programming at the intersection of scholarship and community engagement. Administratively, the Centres fall within Luther’s finance and administration portfolio, which supports their operations. Our largest centre is The Glebe Counselling Centre, a not-for-profit, multifaith counselling agency committed to strengthening emotional and spiritual well-being.

new_jobs.title: Director, Digital Marketing & Web Experience
new_jobs.description:
At Varicent, We’re Not Just Transforming The Sales Performance Management (SPM) Market—we’re Redefining How Organizations Achieve Revenue Success. Our Cutting-edge SaaS Solutions Empower Revenue Leaders Globally To Design Smarter Go-to-market Strategies, Maximize Seller Performance, And Unlock Untapped Potential. Varicent Stands At The Forefront Of Innovation, Celebrated As a Market Leader In The 2025 Forrester Wave Report For SPM, 2023 Ventana Research Revenue Performance Management (RPM) Value Index, Gartner Peer Insights, 2024 Gartner SPM Market Guide, And G2. Our Solutions Are Trusted By a Diverse Range Of Global Industry Leaders Like T-Mobile, ServiceNow, Wawanesa Bank, Shaw Industries, Moody's, Stryker And Hundreds More. Here’s Why You’ll Thrive At Varicent

Innovate with Purpose: Build impactful solutions for customers worldwide.
Join Excellence: Work in a diverse, collaborative, and innovative team.
Shape the Future: Lead in redefining revenue optimization.
Grow Together: Unlock your potential in a supportive environment.

Join us at Varicent—where your talent and ambition meet limitless opportunities for success!

The Opportunity

We’re looking for a Director, Digital Marketing & Web Experience
to lead how Varicent attracts, engages, and converts buyers across our digital ecosystem.

This is a high-impact leadership role for someone who loves connecting strategy with execution. You’ll own our digital growth strategy across paid media, web experience, SEO/AEO/GEO, conversion optimization, and performance measurement
, with a clear focus on generating pipeline and supporting revenue growth.

You’ll have the opportunity to shape the function — leading a Senior Manager of Digital Marketing and Senior Web Developer
, partnering with specialized agencies, and working closely with senior leaders across Marketing, Sales, Revenue Operations, Product Marketing, Content, Creative, and Finance.

We’re looking for someone who is comfortable setting the vision while staying close enough to the work to know what’s performing, what isn’t, and where we should move next.

What You’ll Do

Own Our Digital Growth Strategy

Set the strategy and roadmap across paid media, website experience, SEO/AEO/GEO, conversion optimization, and digital acquisition.
Connect digital investments directly to business goals, including pipeline, revenue, customer acquisition, and brand growth.
Identify new opportunities across buyer behavior, emerging channels, AI-powered search, personalization, and digital experiences.
Bring together teams, agencies, technology, and data around clear priorities and measurable outcomes.

Turn Our Website Into a Growth Engine

Own the strategy for Varicent.com as a key demand generation, storytelling, and conversion platform.
Partner closely with our Senior Web Developer to evolve the website experience, UX, navigation, performance, accessibility, and conversion paths.
Use analytics, behavioral insights, A/B testing, and experimentation to continuously improve the buyer journey.
Lead major web initiatives such as redesigns, personalization, CMS improvements, and other digital experience programs.

Drive Digital Acquisition & Discoverability

Lead our paid media strategy across search, social, retargeting, ABM, programmatic, and other digital channels.
Own channel mix, budget allocation, forecasting, and optimization based on performance.
Shape Varicent’s approach to SEO, AEO, and GEO, helping buyers discover us across both traditional and AI-powered search experiences.
Partner with Demand Generation, Product Marketing, and Content to translate campaigns into effective digital experiences.

Make Data Actionable

Define how we measure digital performance across traffic, engagement, conversion, opportunities, pipeline, and ROI.
Partner with Marketing Operations and Revenue Operations to strengthen tracking, attribution, lead flow, and reporting.
Turn performance data into clear recommendations on where to optimize, experiment, and invest.
Build a culture of testing and continuous improvement across channels, audiences, creative, and web experiences.

Lead & Build

Lead and develop a Senior Manager of Digital Marketing and Senior Web Developer, alongside our paid media and SEO/AEO/GEO agency partners.
Create clear priorities and operating rhythms that allow the team to move quickly without sacrificing quality.
Own digital marketing and web budgets, agency relationships, tools, and investments.
Serve as a trusted digital strategy partner to the SVP of Marketing and broader Marketing leadership team.
Help shape how the digital and web function evolves as Varicent grows.

What You’ll Bring

We’re looking for a digital leader who has operated in a B2B SaaS, technology, enterprise software, or similarly complex sales environment
and understands how digital experiences translate into business growth.

You’ll Likely Bring

12+ years of experience across digital marketing, growth, demand generation, performance marketing, or web strategy.
7+ years of people leadership experience, including leading multidisciplinary teams or managers.
Experience owning digital strategy with measurable responsibility for pipeline, revenue, conversion, and customer acquisition.
Deep knowledge of paid media, SEO/SEM, digital acquisition, web strategy, CRO, analytics, and experimentation.
Experience owning or significantly influencing a B2B website and understanding how UX, content, technology, and conversion work together.
Experience managing meaningful digital budgets and making investment decisions based on performance.
Strong analytical instincts and the ability to turn complex data into clear recommendations.
Experience leading agencies and external partners while maintaining strong internal ownership.
The ability to influence senior stakeholders, navigate competing priorities, and connect digital strategy to broader company goals.
Comfort working in a growth-oriented environment where priorities evolve and leaders are expected to both set direction and help move the work forward.
Familiarity with tools such as HubSpot, Google Ads, GA4, Google Tag Manager, Salesforce, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, ABM platforms, experimentation tools, and modern analytics platforms.
An understanding of how AI is changing digital marketing, content discovery, personalization, and the buyer journey.

Nice to Have

Experience with HubSpot CMS, ABM and intent platforms, multi-touch attribution, website personalization, CRO platforms, behavioral analytics, major website redesigns or migrations, and global digital programs
is a plus.

Working knowledge of HTML/CSS and familiarity with accessibility, privacy, Core Web Vitals, and web governance will also help you partner effectively with our web team.

What Success Looks Like

In your first few months, you’ll get to know our digital ecosystem, team, agencies, performance, and buyers; identify where we can improve quickly; and establish clear priorities for digital growth.

From there, you’ll build a multi-quarter roadmap, strengthen how we measure digital contribution to pipeline and revenue, establish a structured experimentation approach, and evolve Varicent’s website into an even stronger growth and conversion engine.

Over time, success will mean better digital experiences, stronger organic visibility, smarter media investment, higher conversion, clearer performance insights, and measurable growth in digital-sourced pipeline
— supported by a team and operating model that can scale with Varicent.

Additional Information

For this role, the estimated annual base salary range is between $138,200.00 - $181,400.00 CAD
. In addition to base salary, our compensation package may include bonuses, commissions for eligible sales roles, and a comprehensive benefits package. The actual base salary will vary based on factors including individual qualifications and market data, as objectively assessed during the interview process.

This posting is for a new vacancy
.

This hiring process utilizes artificial intelligence tools to assist in candidate screening and assessment. Our AI tools are designed to complement — not replace — human decision-making.

Overview Of Benefits

Health & Wellness — Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage tailored to your local needs
Time Off — PTO and public holidays to rest, recharge, and do what matters most
Volunteer Days — Dedicated time to give back and support the communities that matter to you
Ignite Days — Dedicated learning days to support continuous growth, skill development, and professional learning
Financial — Compensation that reflects your market and your value
Retirement — Retirement plans designed to help you build long-term financial security
Tuition Assistance — Invest in your growth with support for continuing education and professional development
Flexibility — Work where you thrive, with remote and hybrid options available across most regions
